173.t: Old parks and the gardeners' picnic at Southern Park
173.s: Allen asks about Crescent Pleasure Park, Southern Park and others; Stecklet recalls the gardeners' picnic and a tomato-growing prize winner.
173.q: Oh, yeah, they used to have a regular lay there. Because the gardeners used to give a picnic there. And when the young girls, their daughter would be, you know, sitting down there, and the fellow would come along, he'd top them on the show and tell them, dance with my daughter and I'll give you a…

173.s: He has no firsthand knowledge of these parks and only guesses their locations.
173.q: Yeah. I remember now. Let's see. Sportsman's Park. I don't think I ever went to anything there, but I, on the door, I know I never played there. But I think that was out on Tulane Avenue.

173.t: Smokey Mary train to the lakefront
173.s: The train to Lake Pontchartrain, where Woodrow's and Washington Garden sat on either side of the track, took half an hour and cost fifteen cents round trip.
173.q: Well, no doubt. Yeah. Because I used to go to them private picnics and then I'd go to Ada Woodrow or Washington Garden and I'd dance till midnight and catch Smokey Mary. They used to call that Smokey Mary. That train used to go out there. And the camellia used to land it, which I showed you the…

620.t: Lincoln, Johnson, Commercial and Southern parks
620.s: He describes the big picnic parks and where Commercial Park and Southern Park stood relative to the bayou.
620.q: Well, they had the Dixit Park, the Lincoln Park. They had the Commercial Park there. On the bayou, they had the Crosswood from there, they had the Southern Park.

620.s: He recalls watching a man go up in a balloon and jump with a crude parachute, and people catching balloons for a dollar.
620.q: Yeah, I remember the... We used to go out there and look at a fellow called... Billy Caillou, I believe it was. He used to go up in that balloon. Jump out that balloon. He had to go up there and then jump out that thing.

620.t: The Bemmel steam train to the lake
620.s: He describes the steam train that ran from Basin and Canal out to the lake, slow, with bands playing on Sundays, when he was six or seven.
620.q: You go in for nothing when you get the ball out to be outside. I remember that good. You see that train? They had a train used to run out to the Spanish food. A bangle train.

254.t: Lincoln Park built on Coleman's old garden square
254.s: He locates Lincoln Park on a whole square formerly Coleman's vegetable garden, built about 1905 with a fence and a big dance hall.
254.q: Now and then, now and then. They didn't start building around that about 1915. I see. Well, we'll start asking about the park, which was right there. Was it, could you tell me where was the park, where the park, Lincoln Park was? Lincoln Park was right there where I lived there by the welfare. And…

254.t: Park attractions, boxing and cleaning up the dance hall
254.s: He describes the Sunday shows and dances, the flying horses, ferris wheel, balloons and boxing, and cleaning the hall for leftover beer as a boy.
254.q: Yeah. Somewhere, no. And that down at the next... That's where the baseball... I mean, uh... Where the... The mountain blue is there now. That's where the... That's where the terrace wheel was. Around... Around... Yeah. The Hanuman Park? That's where the Hanuman Park used to be. Yeah. I see. Did…

22.t: White City amusement park on Tulane Avenue
22.s: He clarifies that White City was a theater and amusement place in Carrollton where his father took the family, later the ballpark site.
22.q: No, they had no...oh, wait a minute. Stop the machine a minute. This was at Tulane Avenue in Carrollton. It was called the White City. They used to give plays there. Or semi-operatic plays and different things. My father used to take us there to listen to the music.

22.t: Shows, drinks and bottled pop at White City
22.s: Hogan asks about the amusements; La Rocca describes burning-city shows, opera bands, soft drinks and the old pop bottles.
22.q: Well, they used to have music in different little plays and shows like the burning of a city. Yeah. And you'd see a cardboard house that built and it had a fire. And some of the girls would hire for about $2 a night. And they'd come jumping out them windows. You understand? And that was bigger…

864.t: Lincoln Park, the skating rink and the gas balloon
864.s: He recalls the old Lincoln Park skating rink and the Sunday gas balloon, which he thinks drew people to the park.
864.ch: Style and old New Orleans customs
864.q: shoddish? Well, we used to have them long years ago, but I never did see them. We had them here though. What is it anyhow? I just heard about them. Well, now there's two kinds. There's a kind you can dance in a hole and there's a car and you dance on ice, with ice skis. But the most of them, the…

182.t: Flag raising and pot go shooting at Razo
182.s: Asked about flag raisings, Tom describes a shooting contest with a decoy on a post near Delacroix, which he did not play for.
182.ch: Playing in the country and Delacroix
182.q: I was playing in the, in the, uh, Razo, and I was playing out there with the string band, and they was, they had a pot go shooting. A what? Pot go. She had a big thing on the, uh, on a pole. And there was good shots there in the country. That was way in the, uh, Razo, they call it. Razo. I know.

779.t: Pelicans ballpark, White City and Charles Bowler's band
779.s: Where the Pelicans and White City were, and playing with Charles Bowler at ballparks, racetrack and parades.
779.q: The Pelicans played on Cleveland and Counting Avenue, around that way somewhere. They had the ballpark there. Yeah. And of course later on they moved to, you know, where they, you know, they're fresh out there on Counting and Tulane.

56.t: The balloon and parachute at Lincoln Park
56.s: A canvas balloon, a parachute and a chimney landing.
56.ch: Lincoln Park and the name Kid
56.q: They played that music in front of them. They were reading everything. They enjoyed back in, you know, guys. Yeah. What did that balloon look like that that that fellow had to do? Yeah. The pavilion, the pavilion, the pavilion. The pavilion.
